text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Spending on Romania's NATO integration would amount to $2.99 billion, or three percent of the gross domestic product, according to estimates by the Political Studies Institute.

- The government is expected to reach a decision on road taxes on Wednesday. National Peasant Party president Ion Diaconescu said the proposed taxes were too high. He said they would range only from 50,000 lei to 400,000.

- Workers at farm machinery maker Semanatoare are still unhappy with an association contract concluded with Italy's New Holland. They went on an one-hour strike on Monday. The State Ownership Fund is in favour of the contract.
- Exports of wheat flour, bread, maize, barley have been liberalised in line with a recent Industry Ministry decree. Exports will not need a licence starting August.

- Foreign investment in Romania in seven years since the fall of communism amounted to $2.48 billion as of May 9, the Romanian Development Agency reported. The Netherlands is the largest single foreign investor with $256.2 million.

- Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara said he was pleased with the results of the meeting with the World Bank president. He said Romania would not have to resort to more loans and could even make savings.
- The Finance Ministry plans to launch treasury bills on the German market at the end of May, Ciumara said.
- Bankcoop commercial bank cut its interest rates on leu deposits starting Monday.
- Romania will get total loans worth $705 million from the World Bank in 1997.
